pr.title: gh-141311: Avoid assertion in BytesIO readinto
pr.body:
Account for when self->pos is equal to PY_SSIZE_T_MAX. The length of read was correctly set to zero but the asserts assumed self->pos couldn't reach PY_SSIZE_T_MAX. Return early to avoid edge cases.

files.patch:
@@ -54,6 +54,12 @@ def testSeek(self):
         self.assertEqual(buf[3:], bytesIo.read())
         self.assertRaises(TypeError, bytesIo.seek, 0.0)
 
+        self.assertEqual(sys.maxsize, bytesIo.seek(sys.maxsize))
+        self.assertEqual(self.EOF, bytesIo.read(4))
+
+        self.assertEqual(sys.maxsize - 2, bytesIo.seek(sys.maxsize - 2))
+        self.assertEqual(self.EOF, bytesIo.read(4))
+
     def testTell(self):
         buf = self.buftype("1234567890")
         bytesIo = self.ioclass(buf)
@@ -552,6 +558,14 @@ def test_relative_seek(self):
         memio.seek(1, 1)
         self.assertEqual(memio.read(), buf[1:])
 
+    def test_issue141311(self):
+        memio = self.ioclass()
+        # Seek allows PY_SSIZE_T_MAX, read should handle that.
+        # Past end of buffer read should always return 0 (EOF).
+        self.assertEqual(sys.maxsize, memio.seek(sys.maxsize))
+        buf = bytearray(2)
+        self.assertEqual(0, memio.readinto(buf))
+
     def test_unicode(self):
         memio = self.ioclass()

@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+Fix assertion failure in :func:`!io.BytesIO.readinto` and undefined behavior
+arising when read position is above capcity in :class:`io.BytesIO`.

review_comments.body:
Isn't it enough to fix this assertion?
```suggestion
    assert(self->pos + len <= PY_SSIZE_T_MAX);
```

+:func:`~io.BufferedIOBase.readinto` when the current offset is at the max
review_comments.body:
> ```in :class:`io.BytesIO` implementation of
:func:`~io.BufferedIOBase.readinto` ```

You can simply write ``` in :meth:`io.BytesIO.readinto` ```.

It will but I worry about the later `PyBytes_AS_STRING(self->buf) + self->pos` as `self->pos` is `PY_SSIZE_T_MAX` and adding a large integer to a pointer then doing a `memcpy` from that computed address (even 0 bytes) feels like a path to undefined behavior to me. Happy to implement whichever you'd prefer.

review_comments.body: That will reference error as the `BytesIO` (https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.BytesIO) doc currently only defines `read1` and `readinto1`.

review_comments.body: Good point. If adding PY_SSIZE_T_MAX causes troubles, adding slightly smaller value will also cause troubles. Actually, if pos larger than the size of the array, ot is an undefined behaviour. So, a specoal case for empty read is needed too.

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+Fix assertion failure in :class:`io.BytesIO` implementation of
+:func:`~io.BufferedIOBase.readinto` when the current offset is at the max
review_comments.body: Then simply use `!`. The method exist, even if there is no anchor for it.
The issue is a "past the end of array", not integer overflow
I do not think this is possible. size=0 if self->pos >= self->string_size.

I afraid that future developers can try to remove this code as "redundant". There is no memory access if `size == 0`. Creating a pointer that points past the array is an undefined behavior in C, even if we do not try to access memory. Could you please make this more clear?

issue_comments.body:
I audited the codepaths which did `self->pos + buffer`.

For `read_bytes_lock_held` the `size` parameter is always set to 0 by calling code currently if `self->pos > self->string_size`. I added a range check for `self->pos` as an extra safety as codepaths change but can remove if it's too much.

`write_bytes_lock_held`: `endpos` is a `size_t` so can hold `2 * PY_SSIZE_T_MAX`. Value is bounds checked in `resize_buffer_lock_held`.

A number of cases use `scan_eol_lock_held` to move forward. That has code which checks `self->pos >= self->string_size` and returns `0`. Callers seem to handle that correctly (early exit or call read_bytes_lock_held)..
